transport_encryption_enabled.title: Transport Encryption Enabled
transport_encryption_enabled.description: Indicates whether the channel uses transport-layer encryption (e.g., TLS/HTTPS) to protect PII in transit. If TLS is not enabled, mTLS is impossible and the exposure is more severe.

protocol_scheme.title: Protocol Scheme
protocol_scheme.description: The application-layer protocol scheme used for PII data transmission.

tls_redirect_enforced.title: TLS Redirect Enforced
tls_redirect_enforced.description: Indicates whether plaintext (non-TLS) connections are automatically redirected to encrypted equivalents (e.g., HTTP to HTTPS redirect with HSTS), preventing any PII from traversing in cleartext.

minimum_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version Enforced
minimum_tls_version.description: The minimum TLS/SSL protocol version the server or client will accept during negotiation. Versions below TLS 1.2 are considered weak and susceptible to downgrade attacks such as POODLE, DROWN, and BEAST.

downgrade_protection_enabled.title: TLS Downgrade Attack Protection Enabled
downgrade_protection_enabled.description: Indicates whether a mechanism to prevent downgrade attacks is active, such as TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV (RFC 7507) or HSTS preloading. Without this, an active adversary can force negotiation to a weaker version.

deprecated_ssl_protocols_enabled.title: Deprecated SSL/TLS Protocols Explicitly Enabled
deprecated_ssl_protocols_enabled.description: List of deprecated protocol versions (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1) that are explicitly enabled in the server or client configuration, increasing attack surface for downgrade exploitation.

allowed_cipher_suites.title: Allowed TLS Cipher Suites
allowed_cipher_suites.description: The list of cipher suites permitted during TLS negotiation, as configured on the server or load balancer.

cipher_suite_policy_enforced.title: Cipher Suite Restriction Policy Enforced
cipher_suite_policy_enforced.description: Whether the server has an explicit allowlist-based cipher suite policy that prevents the use of weak or deprecated ciphers, rather than relying on library defaults.

certificate_chain_validation_enabled.title: Certificate Chain Validation Enabled
certificate_chain_validation_enabled.description: Whether the client enforces full X.509 certificate chain validation against trusted CA roots when establishing TLS connections.

hostname_verification_enabled.title: Hostname Verification Enabled
hostname_verification_enabled.description: Whether the client verifies that the server certificate subject/SAN matches the hostname being connected to.

certificate_revocation_check_mode.title: Certificate Revocation Check Mode
certificate_revocation_check_mode.description: The method used by the client to check whether server certificates have been revoked.

self_signed_certificates_accepted.title: Self-Signed Certificates Accepted
self_signed_certificates_accepted.description: Whether the client explicitly accepts self-signed certificates that are not issued by a trusted CA, bypassing chain validation.

mutual_tls_required.title: Mutual TLS Required
mutual_tls_required.description: Whether the server enforces client certificate authentication during TLS handshake (mTLS). True means client certificates are required and validated.

replay_protection_mechanism.title: Replay Protection Mechanism
replay_protection_mechanism.description: The mechanism used to prevent replay attacks on PII-bearing messages. Nonces are single-use random values, sequence numbers are monotonically increasing counters, timestamps require strict validation windows, and none means no replay protection is in place.

server_side_replay_validation_enforced.title: Server-Side Replay Validation Enforced
server_side_replay_validation_enforced.description: Indicates whether the server actually validates replay protection tokens (nonces, sequence numbers, or timestamps) and rejects duplicate or out-of-window requests.

request_idempotency_key_required.title: Idempotency Key Required
request_idempotency_key_required.description: Indicates whether the API enforces a client-supplied idempotency key validated server-side to prevent duplicate processing of PII-bearing requests.

app_layer_integrity_mechanism.title: Application-Layer Integrity Mechanism
app_layer_integrity_mechanism.description: The application-layer mechanism used to ensure message integrity beyond transport-layer protections (e.g., HMAC, digital signatures, or none).

tls_terminated_at_intermediary.title: TLS Terminated at Intermediary
tls_terminated_at_intermediary.description: Indicates whether TLS is terminated at an intermediary (e.g., load balancer or reverse proxy) before the traffic reaches the backend application.

backend_transport_reencrypted.title: Backend Transport Re-encrypted
backend_transport_reencrypted.description: Whether the connection from the intermediary to the backend application is re-encrypted with TLS after termination at the intermediary.

hsts_header_present.title: HSTS Header Present
hsts_header_present.description: Whether the application sets the Strict-Transport-Security HTTP response header on HTTPS responses.

hsts_max_age_seconds.title: HSTS max-age Value (Seconds)
hsts_max_age_seconds.description: The max-age directive value in seconds from the Strict-Transport-Security header. A value of 0 disables HSTS. NIST and OWASP recommend at least 31536000 (1 year).

http_plaintext_accessible.title: HTTP Plaintext Endpoint Accessible
http_plaintext_accessible.description: Whether the application accepts or responds to connections on unencrypted HTTP (port 80 or equivalent) without redirecting to HTTPS, enabling interception before TLS upgrade.

rate_limiting_enabled.title: Rate Limiting Enabled
rate_limiting_enabled.description: Whether request rate limiting or bandwidth throttling controls are enforced on this PII data channel (e.g., via API gateway policies, middleware, WAF rules, or application-level controls).

channel_authentication_required.title: Channel Authentication Required
channel_authentication_required.description: Whether the channel requires authentication before data access is permitted. Unauthenticated channels with no rate limiting present a higher exfiltration and enumeration risk.

bulk_export_endpoint_exposed.title: Bulk Export Endpoint Exposed
bulk_export_endpoint_exposed.description: Whether the channel exposes endpoints that allow bulk or paginated retrieval of PII records without per-request limits, increasing the risk of large-scale data harvesting.

rpki_route_origin_validation_enabled.title: RPKI Route Origin Validation Enabled
rpki_route_origin_validation_enabled.description: Whether RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) Route Origin Validation is enforced on BGP sessions to cryptographically verify that announcing ASes are authorized to originate their prefixes, preventing prefix hijacking.

traffic_path_uses_private_interconnect.title: Traffic Path Uses Private Interconnect
traffic_path_uses_private_interconnect.description: Whether PII-bearing traffic between client and application traverses a private interconnect (e.g., dedicated leased line, AWS Direct Connect, Azure ExpressRoute, SD-WAN with private backbone) rather than the public internet BGP routing fabric.

transport_encryption_enforced.title: Transport Encryption Enforced End-to-End
transport_encryption_enforced.description: Whether strong transport-layer encryption (TLS 1.2+ or equivalent) is enforced end-to-end for PII in transit, such that even if traffic is redirected via BGP hijacking, payload contents remain confidential and integrity-protected.

dnssec_validation_enabled.title: DNSSEC Validation Enabled
dnssec_validation_enabled.description: Whether the client DNS resolver enforces DNSSEC validation for the application endpoint domain, preventing acceptance of unsigned or spoofed DNS responses.

dns_over_encrypted_transport.title: DNS over Encrypted Transport (DoH/DoT)
dns_over_encrypted_transport.description: Whether DNS queries for the application endpoint are sent over an encrypted channel such as DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) or DNS-over-TLS (DoT), preventing network-level interception and manipulation of DNS traffic.

certificate_pinning_enabled.title: TLS Certificate Pinning Enabled
certificate_pinning_enabled.description: Whether the client application enforces certificate pinning for the application endpoint, providing a compensating control that would cause the TLS handshake to fail even if DNS was spoofed to an adversary-controlled server presenting a fraudulent certificate.
